To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ash1 mRNA, which encodes a protein that specifies cell fate, is localized to the daughter bud tip in a Myo4p-dependent manner, and that the 3' untranslated sequence is essential for the localization.

Ash1 mRNA, like mRNAs encoding proteins that are asymmetrically localized in higher eukaries, is localized to the daughter bud, and this localization requires the 3' untranslated sequence of Ash1 mRNA and the actin and myosin cytoskeleton.

(1) Ash1 mRNA is associated with the actin cytoplasm in the distal tip region of the bud; (2) Ash1 mRNA localization is independent of its 5' UTR; (3) Ash1 mRNA particles associate with the cell membrane; and (4) Ash1 mRNA transport requires the myosin motor protein, Myo4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of RNA localization in yeast.
the mechanisms by which the cell cycle is controlled and how this is linked with the development of the cell.
the localization of messenger RNA in budding yeast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ash1 mRNA is transported into the daughter cell by actin filaments.
In this report, the authors demonstrate that Ash1 mRNA localization in yeast is dependent on the 3' UTR of the mRNA and on the presence of the actin and myosin cytoskeleton.
the localization of Ash1 mRNA in yeast is a novel mechanism to ensure asymmetric distribution of a cell-fate determining protein.

Ash1 mRNA localization requires actin cytoskelton and Myo4, and is regulated by Bni1.
we have shown that Ash1 mRNA, a determinant of cell fate in budding yeast, localizes to the distal bud tip by a mechanism involving the actin cytokeleton.

The main takeaway from our work is that
RNA localization is a conserved mechanism in the regulation of cell fate.
Ash1 mRNA localization is dependent on the actin cytoplasmic skeleton, and that the localization of the mRNA depends on the actin motor Myo4.
RNA localization is not a unique property of metazoa.
